# Preferred model and SPEI (PWT x CRU TS)

SPEI, the Standardized Precipitation-Evapotranspiration Index (CSIC SPEIbase,
from the Weighted Climate Dataset with population-density weights at base year
2000), is the standardized climatic water balance, precipitation minus
potential evapotranspiration, accumulated over 1, 12 or 36 months. SPEIbase is
computed from CRU TS, so this section uses PWT x CRU TS, whose temperature and
precipitation deviations come from the same data. SPEI is monthly; the annual
indicators are

- SPEI1, annual mean: the mean of the twelve monthly 1-month values;
- SPEI12, December: the water balance of the calendar year;
- SPEI36, December: the water balance of the three calendar years to December.

Like the deviations, each is demeaned (each country's mean and linear and
quadratic trend removed, on the years from `r params$start_year` minus ten to
the last year of the panel) before its arms are cut, S- = max(-S, 0) (dry) and
S+ = max(S, 0) (wet). Each enters the preferred model in two forms, interacted
with the long-run precipitation as the precipitation deviations are:

```text
signed SPEI:  c S + d S x clim_RR
SPEI arms:    c+ S+ + c- S- + (d+ S+ + d- S-) x clim_RR
```

All models on the same rows: the PWT x CRU TS sample (outliers dropped) with
every SPEI indicator.

```{r spei}
SPEI_INDICATORS <- c(spei1 = "SPEI1, annual mean", spei12 = "SPEI12, December",
                     spei36 = "SPEI36, December")
SPEI_FORMS <- c("signed", "arms")

# Monthly SPEI by country (cached on disk by wcd_get()).
spei_monthly <- function(variable) {
  x <- wcd_get(variable = variable, source = "CSIC", geo_resolution = "gadm0",
               weight = CLIMATE_WEIGHT, weight_year = CLIMATE_WEIGHT_YEAR,
               time_frequency = "monthly", verbose = FALSE)
  tibble::tibble(GID_0 = x$GID_0, year = as.integer(format(x$date, "%Y")),
                 month = as.integer(format(x$date, "%m")), value = x[[3]])
}
spei_december <- function(variable, name) {
  spei_monthly(variable) %>% filter(month == 12) %>% transmute(GID_0, year, !!name := value)
}
spei_raw <- spei_monthly("SPEI1") %>%
  group_by(GID_0, year) %>%
  summarise(spei1 = if (sum(!is.na(value)) == 12) mean(value) else NA_real_, .groups = "drop") %>%
  full_join(spei_december("SPEI12", "spei12"), by = c("GID_0", "year")) %>%
  full_join(spei_december("SPEI36", "spei36"), by = c("GID_0", "year"))

cru <- national_panels[[match("PWT x CRU TS", vapply(national_panels, `[[`, "", "label"))]]

# Availability: the SPEI series, and the PWT x CRU TS country-years they cover.
bind_rows(lapply(names(SPEI_INDICATORS), function(k) {
  have <- spei_raw[!is.na(spei_raw[[k]]), ]
  covered <- paste(cru$clean$GID_0, cru$clean$year) %in% paste(have$GID_0, have$year)
  tibble::tibble(indicator = SPEI_INDICATORS[[k]], first_year = min(have$year),
                 last_year = max(have$year), countries = n_distinct(have$GID_0),
                 sample_rows = nrow(cru$clean), rows_with_spei = sum(covered),
                 countries_without = paste(sort(unique(cru$clean$GID_0[!covered])),
                                           collapse = ", "))
})) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("SPEI (CSIC SPEIbase, WCD, population density 2000): availability",
                               "and coverage of the PWT x CRU TS sample"))

# Demeaned SPEI (each country's mean and quadratic trend removed, as the
# deviations) and its arms.
spei <- spei_raw %>% filter(year >= START_YEAR - MAX_LAGS, year <= cru$end_year)
for (k in names(SPEI_INDICATORS)) {
  ok <- which(is.finite(spei[[k]]))
  sub <- data.frame(GID_1 = spei$GID_0[ok], t = spei$year[ok] - 1990L, x = spei[[k]][ok])
  sub$t2 <- sub$t^2
  m <- fixest::feols(x ~ 1 | GID_1[t, t2], sub, notes = FALSE)
  demeaned <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(spei))
  demeaned[ok[fixest::obs(m)]] <- stats::resid(m)
  spei[[k]] <- demeaned
  spei[[paste0(k, "_dry")]] <- pmax(-demeaned, 0)
  spei[[paste0(k, "_wet")]] <- pmax(demeaned, 0)
}

spei_data <- add_deviation_terms(cru$clean, PREFERRED_SUFFIX) %>%
  inner_join(spei, by = c("GID_0", "year")) %>%
  filter(if_all(all_of(names(SPEI_INDICATORS)), ~ !is.na(.x)))

# Correlations of the demeaned indicators with the deviations (same rows).
stats::cor(as.data.frame(spei_data)[, c(names(SPEI_INDICATORS), "devRR", "devTM")]) %>%
  round(2) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("PWT x CRU TS: correlations of the demeaned SPEI indicators and",
                               "deviations (dP = devRR, dT = devTM)"))

spei_terms <- function(k, form) {
  x <- if (form == "signed") k else paste0(k, c("_dry", "_wet"))
  c(x, paste0(x, ":clim_RR"))
}
spei_models <- c(
  list("Preferred" = fit_model(preferred_terms, spei_data)),
  unlist(lapply(names(SPEI_INDICATORS), function(k) {
    stats::setNames(lapply(SPEI_FORMS, function(f) {
      fit_model(c(preferred_terms, spei_terms(k, f)), spei_data)
    }), paste0(SPEI_INDICATORS[[k]], ", ", SPEI_FORMS))
  }), recursive = FALSE)
)
stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(spei_models, stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)

tibble::tibble(
  model = names(spei_models),
  within_r2 = vapply(spei_models, function(m) fixest::fitstat(m, "wr2")[[1]], 0),
  aic_vs_preferred = vapply(spei_models, stats::AIC, 0) - stats::AIC(spei_models[[1]]),
  spei_p = vapply(spei_models, function(m) {
    if (any(startsWith(names(stats::coef(m)), "spei"))) wald_p(m, "^spei") else NA_real_
  }, 0),
  temperature_p = vapply(spei_models, function(m) wald_p(m, "^devTM"), 0),
  precipitation_p = vapply(spei_models, function(m) wald_p(m, "^devRR"), 0)
) %>%
  mutate(within_r2 = round(within_r2, 4), aic_vs_preferred = round(aic_vs_preferred, 1),
         across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0("PWT x CRU TS, ", stats::nobs(spei_models[[1]]),
                                " country-years: the preferred model with each SPEI indicator; ",
                                "AIC relative to the preferred model; joint tests (p) of the SPEI, ",
                                "temperature and precipitation terms"))

SPEI_DICT <- c(DICT, stats::setNames(
  paste0(rep(c("SPEI1", "SPEI12", "SPEI36"), each = 3), c("", " dry", " wet")),
  paste0(rep(names(SPEI_INDICATORS), each = 3), c("", "_dry", "_wet"))
))
etable(spei_models[c("Preferred", paste0(SPEI_INDICATORS, ", arms"))],
       headers = c("Preferred", "SPEI1", "SPEI12", "SPEI36"), dict = SPEI_DICT, drop = DROP,
       order = c("%^devTM", "%^devRR", "%^spei", "%^conflict"), fitstat = FITSTAT,
       title = "PWT x CRU TS: the preferred model and SPEI arms")

# Effect of SPEI = x at the long-run precipitation of EVAL_CLIMATE$RR.
SPEI_AT <- c(-2, 2)
spei_effects <- function(model, k, form, label) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  m <- EVAL_CLIMATE$RR
  grid <- expand.grid(level = seq_along(m), x = SPEI_AT)
  G <- t(mapply(function(g, x) {
    w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
    values <- if (form == "signed") {
      stats::setNames(x, k)
    } else {
      stats::setNames(c(max(-x, 0), max(x, 0)), paste0(k, c("_dry", "_wet")))
    }
    for (term in names(values)) {
      w[[term]] <- values[[term]]
      w[[interaction_name(term, "clim_RR", terms)]] <- values[[term]] * m[[g]]
    }
    w
  }, grid$level, grid$x))
  colnames(G) <- terms
  linear_combination(model, G) %>%
    mutate(model = label, column = sprintf("SPEI %+d, %s", grid$x, EVAL_LABELS$RR[grid$level]),
           p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)))
}
bind_rows(lapply(names(SPEI_INDICATORS), function(k) {
  bind_rows(lapply(SPEI_FORMS, function(f) {
    label <- paste0(SPEI_INDICATORS[[k]], ", ", f)
    spei_effects(spei_models[[label]], k, f, label)
  }))
})) %>%
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * estimate, stars(p_value))) %>%
  select(model, column, cell) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Effect of SPEI of -2 (extremely dry) and +2 (extremely wet) on",
                               "growth (pp) at long-run precipitation of 0.5, 1.5 and 3 m;",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

# The temperature and precipitation deviations with and without SPEI.
significance_map(bind_rows(lapply(names(spei_models), function(k) {
  climate_effects(list(preferred = spei_models[[k]], panel = list(label = k)))
}))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Effect of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp) without and with SPEI;",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

# 20-year deviations with the baseline fixed during runs

With a trailing baseline, a sequence of warm years raises the baseline as it
goes, so each later warm year looks less anomalous than the first. The
run-fixed deviation (as `add_climate_runs()` in functions/climate_runs.R, there
for temperature) holds the trailing mean and SD at their value at the start of
the run:

- a warming run is a maximal sequence of at least two consecutive years with
  strictly rising temperature; position 1 is the year before the first rise.
  Cooling runs are the same with falling temperature, so a peak or trough ends
  one run and starts the other;
- within a run, the deviation uses the trailing 20-year mean and SD of its
  position-1 year; outside runs (and at position 1), the moving ones;
- the warm arm is cut from the warming-run deviation, the cold arm from the
  cooling-run deviation.

Precipitation is treated the same way, with wetting (rising) and drying
(falling) runs. The run-fixed deviations are demeaned as the others (each
unit's mean and quadratic trend removed) before their arms are cut. The model:
20-year deviations, quadratic arms for temperature and linear arms for
precipitation, interacted with the horizon mean, as in the selection table; the
moving and run-fixed versions on the same rows.

```{r run-fixed-baseline}
RUN_FORM <- "T quadratic, P linear arms"
RUN_DEFINITION <- "20-year"
RUN_DIRECTIONS <- c(up = 1, down = -1)

# Each unit's mean and linear and quadratic trend removed from x (as the
# deviations of prepare_panel()), on the finite values.
demean_unit_trend <- function(unit, year, x) {
  ok <- which(is.finite(x))
  sub <- data.frame(GID_1 = unit[ok], t = year[ok] - 1990L, x = x[ok])
  sub$t2 <- sub$t^2
  m <- fixest::feols(x ~ 1 | GID_1[t, t2], sub, notes = FALSE)
  out <- rep(NA_real_, length(x))
  out[ok[fixest::obs(m)]] <- stats::resid(m)
  out
}

# Deviation of variable v from its trailing moments (`baseline`), with the
# moments held at their position-1 values through each rising (direction 1)
# or falling (-1) run of v; outside runs, the moving deviation. The run
# identifiers are those of add_climate_runs() (.run_ids()).
run_fixed_deviation <- function(data, v, direction, baseline = "lag_20") {
  mean_col <- paste0("mean_", v, "_", baseline)
  sd_col <- paste0("sd_", v, "_", baseline)
  data %>%
    group_by(GID_1) %>%
    arrange(year, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
    mutate(change = if_else(year == dplyr::lag(year) + 1L,
                            .data[[v]] - dplyr::lag(.data[[v]]), NA_real_),
           run_id = .run_ids(change, direction)) %>%
    group_by(GID_1, run_id) %>%
    mutate(in_run = !is.na(run_id) & n() >= 2L,
           position = if_else(in_run, row_number(), 1L),
           mean_fixed = if_else(in_run, first(.data[[mean_col]]), .data[[mean_col]]),
           sd_fixed = if_else(in_run, first(.data[[sd_col]]), .data[[sd_col]]),
           deviation = (.data[[v]] - mean_fixed) / sd_fixed) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(GID_1, year, position, deviation)
}

# The panel's clean rows with the demeaned fixed-baseline deviations of each
# variable and direction from `fixed_deviation` (dm_<v>_<tag><direction>) and
# the positions in the runs or spells (position_<v>_<tag>_<direction>).
add_run_fixed <- function(panel, fixed_deviation = run_fixed_deviation, tag = "run") {
  data <- panel$data %>%
    filter(year >= START_YEAR - MAX_LAGS, year <= panel$end_year, !is.na(TM), !is.na(RR))
  out <- data %>% select(GID_1, year)
  for (v in c("TM", "RR")) for (dir in names(RUN_DIRECTIONS)) {
    x <- fixed_deviation(data, v, RUN_DIRECTIONS[[dir]])
    x[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", tag, dir)]] <- demean_unit_trend(x$GID_1, x$year, x$deviation)
    names(x)[names(x) == "position"] <- paste0("position_", v, "_", tag, "_", dir)
    out <- left_join(out, select(x, -deviation), by = c("GID_1", "year"))
  }
  # A run that starts before the trailing moments exist has no fixed baseline;
  # those rows are left out, for the moving baseline too.
  fixed_columns <- paste0("dm_", rep(c("TM", "RR"), each = 2), "_", tag, names(RUN_DIRECTIONS))
  panel$clean %>%
    inner_join(out, by = c("GID_1", "year")) %>%
    filter(if_all(all_of(fixed_columns), is.finite))
}

# The deviation terms of the 20-year definition, with the arms of `fixed`
# variables cut from the fixed-baseline deviations (warm or wet arm from the
# rising runs or warm spells, cold or dry arm from the falling runs or cold
# spells).
run_fixed_terms <- function(model_data, fixed = c("TM", "RR"), tag = "run") {
  d <- add_deviation_terms(model_data, DEFINITIONS[[RUN_DEFINITION]])
  for (v in fixed) {
    up <- model_data[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", tag, "up")]]
    down <- model_data[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", tag, "down")]]
    d[[paste0("dev", v, "_pos")]] <- pmax(up, 0)
    d[[paste0("dev", v, "_neg")]] <- pmax(-down, 0)
    d[[paste0("dev", v, "_pos2")]] <- pmax(up, 0)^2
    d[[paste0("dev", v, "_neg2")]] <- pmax(-down, 0)^2
  }
  d
}
# The variants: which variables have the fixed baseline ("<label>-fixed T and
# P", "... T", "... P"), against the moving baseline.
run_variants <- function(label) {
  stats::setNames(list(character(0), c("TM", "RR"), "TM", "RR"),
                  c("Moving baseline", paste0(label, "-fixed ", c("T and P", "T", "P"))))
}

# 1. How often and how much the fixed baseline changes the deviation, on the
# rows `d` (names: the rising and falling sequences of each variable).
fixed_change_table <- function(d, tag, names_TM, names_RR, what) {
  moving <- add_deviation_terms(d, DEFINITIONS[[RUN_DEFINITION]])
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    sequence_names <- if (v == "TM") names_TM else names_RR
    bind_rows(lapply(names(RUN_DIRECTIONS), function(dir) {
      fixed <- d[[paste0("dm_", v, "_", tag, dir)]]
      position <- d[[paste0("position_", v, "_", tag, "_", dir)]]
      later <- position >= 2
      arm <- if (dir == "up") pmax(fixed, 0) else pmax(-fixed, 0)
      arm_moving <- moving[[paste0("dev", v, if (dir == "up") "_pos" else "_neg")]]
      tibble::tibble(variable = v, sequence = sequence_names[[dir]],
                     share_at_position_2_plus = mean(later),
                     share_at_position_5_plus = mean(position >= 5),
                     mean_change_at_2_plus = mean((fixed - moving[[paste0("dev", v)]])[later]),
                     arm_above_2sd_moving = sum(arm_moving > 2), arm_above_2sd_fixed = sum(arm > 2),
                     correlation = stats::cor(fixed, moving[[paste0("dev", v)]]))
    }))
  })) %>%
    mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3))) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
      main$label, ": country-years at ", what, " position 2 or later and 5 or later, mean ",
      "change of the demeaned deviation from position 2 (fixed minus moving, SD), arm values ",
      "above 2 SD, and the correlation of the two deviations"))
}

# 2. The model with moving and fixed baselines on the main panel (same rows):
# fit and joint tests, effects, and coefficients (printed by the caller, so
# that knitr renders the tables).
fixed_model_tables <- function(d, tag, label) {
  models <- lapply(run_variants(label), function(fixed) {
    fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[RUN_FORM]]), run_fixed_terms(d, fixed, tag))
  })
  stopifnot(length(unique(vapply(models, stats::nobs, 0))) == 1)
  list(
    fit = fit_summary(models) %>%
      mutate(aic_vs_moving = round(aic - aic[1], 1), within_r2 = round(within_r2, 4),
             across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
      select(-aic, -bic) %>%
      knitr::kable(caption = paste0(main$label, ": ", RUN_FORM, ", ", RUN_DEFINITION,
                                    " deviations, moving and ", tolower(label), "-fixed ",
                                    "baselines; joint tests (p) and AIC relative to the moving ",
                                    "baseline")),
    effects = significance_map(bind_rows(lapply(names(models), function(k) {
      climate_effects(list(preferred = models[[k]], panel = list(label = k)), RUN_FORM)
    }))) %>%
      knitr::kable(caption = paste0(main$label, ": effect of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp), moving ",
                                    "and ", tolower(label), "-fixed baselines; *** p < 0.01, ",
                                    "** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1")),
    coefficients = etable(models, dict = DICT, drop = DROP, order = ORDER, fitstat = FITSTAT,
                          title = paste0(main$label, ": ", RUN_FORM, " with moving and ",
                                         tolower(label), "-fixed baselines"))
  )
}

# 3. Moving against fixed (T and P) on every national panel.
RUN_CELLS <- c("T +3 SD, 25 °C", "T -3 SD, 5 °C", "P -3 SD, 0.5 m", "P -3 SD, 1.5 m")
fixed_panel_table <- function(panel_data, tag, label) {
  variants <- run_variants(label)[1:2]
  bind_rows(lapply(names(panel_data), function(p) {
    bind_rows(lapply(names(variants), function(k) {
      m <- fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[RUN_FORM]]),
                     run_fixed_terms(panel_data[[p]], variants[[k]], tag))
      effects <- significance_map(climate_effects(list(preferred = m, panel = list(label = p)),
                                                  RUN_FORM))
      tibble::tibble(panel = p, baseline = k, aic = stats::AIC(m),
                     temperature_p = wald_p(m, "^devTM"),
                     precipitation_p = wald_p(m, "^devRR")) %>%
        bind_cols(select(effects, all_of(RUN_CELLS)))
    }))
  })) %>%
    group_by(panel) %>%
    mutate(aic_vs_moving = round(aic - aic[1], 1)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(panel, baseline, aic_vs_moving, temperature_p, precipitation_p, all_of(RUN_CELLS)) %>%
    mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
    knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
      "Every national panel: ", RUN_FORM, ", ", RUN_DEFINITION, " deviations, moving against ",
      tolower(label), "-fixed (T and P) baselines; joint tests (p), AIC relative to the moving ",
      "baseline, and effects of a +/-3 SD deviation (pp); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
}

run_data <- lapply(national_panels, add_run_fixed)
names(run_data) <- vapply(national_panels, `[[`, "", "label")
fixed_change_table(run_data[[main$label]], "run", c(up = "warming run", down = "cooling run"),
                   c(up = "wetting run", down = "drying run"), "run")
run_tables <- fixed_model_tables(run_data[[main$label]], "run", "Run")
run_tables$fit
run_tables$effects
run_tables$coefficients
fixed_panel_table(run_data, "run", "Run")
```

## Fixed during spells above or below the baseline

A spell is a sequence of years on the same side of the baseline, rather than of
rising (falling) years: a warm spell starts in a year above its trailing
20-year mean, and the baseline (mean and SD) is held at that year's value for
as long as the following years stay above it; it ends with the first year at or
below the held mean (or a gap), and the next year starts afresh from its own
trailing moments. Membership is judged against the held baseline, so the rising
trailing mean cannot end a spell by itself. Cold, wet and dry spells are the
same, below or above. The first year of a spell has its moving deviation; the
warm (wet) arm is cut from the warm-spell deviation and the cold (dry) arm from
the cold-spell one, demeaned as before. Everything else as above.

```{r spell-fixed-baseline}
# Deviation of x from its trailing moments (mu, s), held at the first year of
# each spell on the `direction` side (1 above, -1 below), and the position in
# the spell (0 outside spells).
fix_spells <- function(x, mu, s, year, direction) {
  n <- length(x)
  deviation <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  position <- integer(n)
  held_mean <- NA_real_
  held_sd <- NA_real_
  p <- 0L
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    continuing <- p > 0L && year[i] == year[i - 1L] + 1L && is.finite(x[i]) &&
      direction * (x[i] - held_mean) > 0
    if (continuing) {
      p <- p + 1L
    } else {
      held_mean <- mu[i]
      held_sd <- s[i]
      p <- if (is.finite(x[i]) && is.finite(held_mean) && direction * (x[i] - held_mean) > 0) 1L else 0L
    }
    deviation[i] <- (x[i] - held_mean) / held_sd
    position[i] <- p
  }
  list(deviation = deviation, position = position)
}
spell_fixed_deviation <- function(data, v, direction, baseline = "lag_20") {
  data <- data[order(data$GID_1, data$year), ]
  deviation <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(data))
  position <- integer(nrow(data))
  for (idx in split(seq_len(nrow(data)), data$GID_1)) {
    r <- fix_spells(data[[v]][idx], data[[paste0("mean_", v, "_", baseline)]][idx],
                    data[[paste0("sd_", v, "_", baseline)]][idx], data$year[idx], direction)
    deviation[idx] <- r$deviation
    position[idx] <- r$position
  }
  tibble::tibble(GID_1 = data$GID_1, year = data$year, position = position,
                 deviation = deviation)
}

spell_data <- lapply(national_panels, add_run_fixed, fixed_deviation = spell_fixed_deviation,
                     tag = "spell")
names(spell_data) <- vapply(national_panels, `[[`, "", "label")
fixed_change_table(spell_data[[main$label]], "spell", c(up = "warm spell", down = "cold spell"),
                   c(up = "wet spell", down = "dry spell"), "spell")
spell_tables <- fixed_model_tables(spell_data[[main$label]], "spell", "Spell")
spell_tables$fit
spell_tables$effects
spell_tables$coefficients
fixed_panel_table(spell_data, "spell", "Spell")
```

# Preferred model and the BHM level terms

The preferred model with the BHM level terms added, on every panel (the same
fixed effects as the preferred model: unit linear and quadratic trends):

```text
growth = deviation terms (preferred model) + b1 TM + b2 TM^2 + b3 RR + b4 RR^2 + controls + FE
```

Does each block still matter given the other? Joint Wald tests of the deviation
terms of each variable and of its BHM terms, alone and together, and the AIC of
the combined model against each alone. In the combined model a deviation of
the year also moves `TM` and `TM^2` (or `RR`, `RR^2`), so its effect is not
the deviation terms alone; the joint tests and the AIC are the comparison.

```{r bhm-preferred}
BHM_TERMS <- c("TM", "TM2", "RR", "RR2")

bhm_comparison <- function(fit) {
  d <- fit$data
  m_bhm <- fit_model(c(BHM_TERMS, CONTROLS), d)
  m_both <- fit_model(c(preferred_terms, BHM_TERMS), d)
  stopifnot(stats::nobs(m_bhm) == stats::nobs(fit$preferred),
            stats::nobs(m_both) == stats::nobs(fit$preferred))
  list(
    models = list("BHM" = m_bhm, "Preferred" = fit$preferred, "Preferred + BHM" = m_both),
    tests = tibble::tibble(
      panel = fit$panel$label,
      dev_T_alone = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devTM"),
      dev_T_with_bhm = wald_p(m_both, "^devTM"),
      bhm_T_alone = wald_p(m_bhm, "^TM2?$"),
      bhm_T_with_dev = wald_p(m_both, "^TM2?$"),
      dev_P_alone = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devRR"),
      dev_P_with_bhm = wald_p(m_both, "^devRR"),
      bhm_P_alone = wald_p(m_bhm, "^RR2?$"),
      bhm_P_with_dev = wald_p(m_both, "^RR2?$"),
      aic_vs_preferred = stats::AIC(m_both) - stats::AIC(fit$preferred),
      aic_vs_bhm = stats::AIC(m_both) - stats::AIC(m_bhm)
    )
  )
}

bhm_comparisons <- lapply(c(national_fits, list(dose_fit)), bhm_comparison)

etable(bhm_comparisons[[1]]$models, dict = DICT, drop = DROP,
       order = c("%^TM$", "%^TM2$", "%^RR$", "%^RR2$", ORDER), fitstat = FITSTAT,
       title = main$label)

bind_rows(lapply(bhm_comparisons, `[[`, "tests")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(starts_with("dev_"), starts_with("bhm_")), ~ signif(.x, 2)),
         across(starts_with("aic_"), ~ round(.x, 1))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Joint Wald tests (p) of the deviation terms (dev) and of the BHM",
                               "terms (bhm) of each variable, alone and with the other block;",
                               "AIC of the combined model minus each alone"))
```

# Preferred model and lagged income

The preferred model with the previous year's log GDP per capita, on every
panel:

```text
growth = deviation terms (preferred model) + h log(GDP per capita)(t-1) + controls + FE
```

With unit fixed effects and trends, `h` is mostly mean reversion within units
(and has the small-T bias of a lagged level with unit effects). Do the
deviation terms survive it?

```{r lagged-income}
lagged_income <- function(fit) {
  d <- mutate(fit$data, lag_log_gdp_pc = lgrp_pc_usd - dlgrp_pc_usd)
  m <- fit_model(c(preferred_terms, "lag_log_gdp_pc"), d)
  stopifnot(stats::nobs(m) == stats::nobs(fit$preferred))
  ct <- fixest::coeftable(m)
  list(
    model = m,
    tests = tibble::tibble(
      panel = fit$panel$label,
      lag_gdp = ct["lag_log_gdp_pc", 1], lag_gdp_se = ct["lag_log_gdp_pc", 2],
      within_r2_without = fixest::fitstat(fit$preferred, "wr2")[[1]],
      within_r2_with = fixest::fitstat(m, "wr2")[[1]],
      T_p_without = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devTM"), T_p_with = wald_p(m, "^devTM"),
      P_p_without = wald_p(fit$preferred, "^devRR"), P_p_with = wald_p(m, "^devRR")
    )
  )
}

income_fits <- lapply(c(national_fits, list(dose_fit)), lagged_income)

bind_rows(lapply(income_fits, `[[`, "tests")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(lag_gdp, lag_gdp_se, within_r2_without, within_r2_with), ~ round(.x, 4)),
         across(ends_with("_without") | ends_with("_with"), ~ signif(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Lagged log GDP per capita: its coefficient, the within R2 and the",
                               "joint tests (p) of each variable's deviation terms without and",
                               "with it"))

income_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(income_fits), function(i) {
  climate_effects(list(preferred = income_fits[[i]]$model,
                       panel = list(label = income_fits[[i]]$tests$panel)))
}))
significance_map(income_effects) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("With lagged log GDP per capita: effect of a +/-3 SD deviation",
                               "(pp) at long-run climates of 5, 15, 25 °C and 0.5, 1.5, 3 m;",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

# Lags of the deviations

Instead of lagged income, the deviation terms of the previous five years, in
the same forms and interacted with the same long-run climate, for both
variables:

```text
growth = sum over k = 0..5 of [ temperature terms(t-k) + precipitation terms(t-k) ] + controls + FE
```

The lags are the deviations of the calendar years before (from every year of
the panel, whether or not it has growth), so a unit-year enters only with all
five lags. The cumulative effect of a deviation through year K is the sum of
its effects on growth in years 0..K, i.e. its effect on the level of GDP per
capita after K years: if a loss is recovered it returns towards zero, if it
persists it stays. The model without lags is re-estimated on the same rows.

Two versions:

- unrestricted: every lag has its own arm coefficients and its own
  interactions with the long-run climate (8 coefficients a lag);
- common interaction: every lag has its own arm coefficients, but each arm has
  one interaction with the long-run climate shared by all lags,

  ```text
  sum over k of [ a+_k dT+(t-k) + a-_k dT-(t-k) ]
    + b+ (sum over k of dT+(t-k)) x clim_TM + b- (sum over k of dT-(t-k)) x clim_TM
  ```

  (and the same for precipitation), so the effect of lag k at long-run climate
  m is `a_k + b m`: the climate shifts the response equally in every year.

  In both, the long-run climate is that of the current year t (with a matched
  20-year interaction, the mean of the 20 years before t, for every lag).
  The test of the restriction is the joint (chi-square) Wald test, in the
  unrestricted model, that each arm's interaction is the same at every lag.

```{r deviation-lags}
# Chi-square Wald test of H b = 0 (clustered VCOV of the model).
wald_linear_p <- function(model, H) {
  b <- stats::coef(model)[colnames(H)]
  V <- stats::vcov(model)[colnames(H), colnames(H)]
  r <- H %*% b
  stat <- as.numeric(t(r) %*% solve(H %*% V %*% t(H)) %*% r)
  stats::pchisq(stat, df = nrow(H), lower.tail = FALSE)
}
# In the unrestricted model: each arm of the variables `vars` has the same
# interaction at every lag (b_k = b_0 for k = 1..N_LAGS).
equal_interactions_p <- function(model, vars) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  rows <- list()
  for (v in vars) for (col in form_columns(v)) {
    climate <- paste0("clim_", v)
    base <- interaction_name(col, climate, terms)
    for (k in seq_len(N_LAGS)) {
      h <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(terms)), terms)
      h[[interaction_name(paste0(col, lag_suffix(k)), climate, terms)]] <- 1
      h[[base]] <- -1
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- h
    }
  }
  wald_linear_p(model, do.call(rbind, rows))
}

distributed_lags <- function(fit) {
  d <- add_deviation_lags(fit)
  all_lags <- unlist(lapply(seq_len(N_LAGS), function(k) c(lag_terms("TM", k), lag_terms("RR", k))))
  m0 <- fit_model(preferred_terms, d)
  m <- fit_model(c(preferred_terms, all_lags), d)
  mr <- fit_model(c(restricted_terms("TM"), restricted_terms("RR"), CONTROLS), d)
  stopifnot(stats::nobs(m0) == stats::nobs(m), stats::nobs(m0) == stats::nobs(mr))
  list(
    panel = fit$panel, no_lags = m0, lags = m, restricted = mr,
    tests = tibble::tibble(
      panel = fit$panel$label, first_year = min(d$year), observations = stats::nobs(m),
      T_p_no_lags = wald_p(m0, "^devTM"), P_p_no_lags = wald_p(m0, "^devRR"),
      T_lags_p = wald_p(m, "^devTM[^:]*_l[0-9]"), P_lags_p = wald_p(m, "^devRR[^:]*_l[0-9]"),
      T_lags_p_common = wald_p(mr, "^devTM[^:]*_l[0-9]"),
      P_lags_p_common = wald_p(mr, "^devRR[^:]*_l[0-9]"),
      equal_T_p = equal_interactions_p(m, "TM"), equal_P_p = equal_interactions_p(m, "RR"),
      aic_lags_vs_no_lags = stats::AIC(m) - stats::AIC(m0),
      aic_common_vs_no_lags = stats::AIC(mr) - stats::AIC(m0)
    )
  )
}

lag_fits <- lapply(c(national_fits, list(dose_fit)), distributed_lags)
lag_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(lag_fits, function(x) {
  cumulative_effects(x$lags, x$panel$label)
}))
common_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(lag_fits, function(x) {
  cumulative_effects(x$restricted, x$panel$label, restricted = TRUE)
}))

lag_tests <- bind_rows(lapply(lag_fits, `[[`, "tests")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(starts_with("T_"), starts_with("P_"), starts_with("equal_")),
                ~ format.pval(signif(.x, 2), eps = 0.001)),
         across(starts_with("aic_"), ~ round(.x, 1)))
lag_tests %>%
  select(panel, first_year, observations, T_p_no_lags, P_p_no_lags, T_lags_p, P_lags_p,
         aic_lags_vs_no_lags) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Unrestricted lags: joint tests (p) of the deviation terms without",
                               "lags and of all the lags of each variable; AIC with lags minus",
                               "without"))
lag_tests %>%
  select(panel, T_lags_p_common, P_lags_p_common, equal_T_p, equal_P_p, aic_common_vs_no_lags,
         aic_lags_vs_no_lags) %>%
  mutate(aic_common_vs_unrestricted = aic_common_vs_no_lags - aic_lags_vs_no_lags) %>%
  select(-aic_lags_vs_no_lags) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Common interaction: joint tests (p) of the lags of each variable;",
                               "test that each arm's interaction is the same at every lag (in",
                               "the unrestricted model); AIC against no lags and against the",
                               "unrestricted lags"))

significance_map(filter(lag_effects, through == 0)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Unrestricted lags: effect in the year of the deviation (pp);",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
significance_map(filter(lag_effects, through == N_LAGS)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Unrestricted lags: cumulative effect over the year of the",
                               "deviation and the five after (pp of GDP per capita); *** p < 0.01,",
                               "** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
significance_map(filter(common_effects, through == 0)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Common interaction: effect in the year of the deviation (pp);",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
significance_map(filter(common_effects, through == N_LAGS)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Common interaction: cumulative effect over the year of the",
                               "deviation and the five after (pp of GDP per capita); *** p < 0.01,",
                               "** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

```{r deviation-lags-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=7}
LAG_CELLS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~variable, ~deviation, ~level_index,
  "TM", 3, 3L, "TM", -3, 3L, "TM", -3, 1L,
  "RR", -3, 1L, "RR", -3, 2L, "RR", 3, 1L
)
plot_lag_paths <- function(effects, version) {
  effects %>%
    semi_join(LAG_CELLS, by = c("variable", "deviation", "level_index")) %>%
    mutate(
      cell = sprintf("%s %+d SD at %s", VARIABLE_LABELS[variable], deviation, level),
      cell = factor(cell, levels = unique(cell)),
      main_panel = panel == main$label,
      panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(panel)),
      across(c(estimate, conf_low, conf_high), ~ 100 * .x)
    ) %>%
    ggplot(aes(through, estimate, colour = panel)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_ribbon(data = function(x) filter(x, main_panel),
                aes(ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high), fill = GRID_PALETTE[[1]], alpha = 0.12,
                colour = NA) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    geom_point(size = 1.4) +
    facet_wrap(~cell, nrow = 2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = stats::setNames(GRID_PALETTE[seq_along(lag_fits)],
                                                 vapply(lag_fits, function(x) x$panel$label, "")),
                        name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Years after the deviation", y = "Cumulative effect on GDP per capita (pp)",
         title = paste("Cumulative effect of a +/-3 SD year over the following years:",
                       version),
         subtitle = paste0(PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations, five lags; ",
                           "band: 95% CI for ", main$label, ".")) +
    theme_results()
}
plot_lag_paths(lag_effects, "unrestricted lags")
plot_lag_paths(common_effects, "common interaction")
```

## Ten lags, common interaction

The common-interaction model with the deviations of the previous ten years,
against the model without lags on the same rows (the ERA5 panels then start in
1970: a 20-year precipitation deviation needs climate from 20 years before).
The confidence intervals of the cumulative effects use the full clustered
covariance of all the lag coefficients.

```{r ten-lags}
common_long_lags <- function(fit) {
  d <- add_deviation_lags(fit, N_LAGS_LONG)
  m0 <- fit_model(preferred_terms, d)
  mr <- fit_model(c(restricted_terms("TM", N_LAGS_LONG), restricted_terms("RR", N_LAGS_LONG),
                    CONTROLS), d)
  stopifnot(stats::nobs(m0) == stats::nobs(mr))
  list(
    panel = fit$panel, model = mr,
    tests = tibble::tibble(
      panel = fit$panel$label, first_year = min(d$year), observations = stats::nobs(mr),
      T_lags_p = wald_p(mr, "^devTM[^:]*_l[0-9]"), P_lags_p = wald_p(mr, "^devRR[^:]*_l[0-9]"),
      aic_vs_no_lags = stats::AIC(mr) - stats::AIC(m0)
    )
  )
}

long_fits <- lapply(c(national_fits, list(dose_fit)), common_long_lags)
long_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(long_fits, function(x) {
  cumulative_effects(x$model, x$panel$label, restricted = TRUE, n_lags = N_LAGS_LONG)
}))

bind_rows(lapply(long_fits, `[[`, "tests")) %>%
  mutate(across(c(T_lags_p, P_lags_p), ~ format.pval(signif(.x, 2), eps = 0.001)),
         aic_vs_no_lags = round(aic_vs_no_lags, 1)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Ten lags, common interaction: joint tests (p) of the lags of each",
                               "variable; AIC minus the model without lags on the same rows"))

significance_map(filter(long_effects, through == 5)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Ten lags, common interaction: cumulative effect through five years",
                               "(pp of GDP per capita); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
significance_map(filter(long_effects, through == N_LAGS_LONG)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Ten lags, common interaction: cumulative effect through ten years",
                               "(pp of GDP per capita); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

```{r ten-lags-plot, fig.width=13, fig.height=7}
plot_lag_paths(long_effects, "ten lags, common interaction") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:N_LAGS_LONG) +
  labs(subtitle = paste0(PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations, ten lags; ",
                         "band: 95% CI for ", main$label, " (full clustered covariance of the ",
                         "lag coefficients)."))
```

# Growth outliers: none, non-weather or all dropped

The preferred model on every panel with no growth outlier dropped, with the
outliers whose cause does not involve weather dropped (the main sample), and
with all of them dropped (the weather-driven ones too). The same country-years
in every panel. For each: the joint tests, the effect of a +/-3 SD deviation in
the year, and the cumulative effects of the dry and hot tails (five
unrestricted lags; ten lags with the common interaction).

```{r outlier-samples}
OUTLIER_SAMPLES <- list(
  "none dropped" = OUTLIERS_ALL[0, ],
  "non-weather dropped" = OUTLIERS_DROPPED,
  "all dropped" = OUTLIERS_ALL
)
outlier_fit <- function(panel, sample) {
  drop <- OUTLIER_SAMPLES[[sample]]
  keep <- !paste(panel$all$GID_0, panel$all$year) %in% paste(drop$GID_0, drop$year)
  d <- add_deviation_terms(panel$all[keep, ], PREFERRED_SUFFIX)
  list(panel = modifyList(panel, list(label = paste0(panel$label, " | ", sample))),
       data = d, preferred = fit_model(preferred_terms, d),
       source_panel = panel$label, sample = sample)
}
outlier_fits <- unlist(lapply(all_panels, function(p) {
  lapply(names(OUTLIER_SAMPLES), function(s) outlier_fit(p, s))
}), recursive = FALSE)

bind_rows(lapply(outlier_fits, function(f) {
  tibble::tibble(panel = f$source_panel, sample = f$sample, rows = stats::nobs(f$preferred),
                 temperature_p = wald_p(f$preferred, "^devTM"),
                 precipitation_p = wald_p(f$preferred, "^devRR"))
})) %>%
  mutate(across(ends_with("_p"), ~ format.pval(signif(.x, 2), eps = 0.001))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Joint tests (p) of each variable's deviation terms by outlier sample")

significance_map(bind_rows(lapply(outlier_fits, climate_effects))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Effect of a +/-3 SD deviation in the year (pp) by outlier sample;",
                               "*** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

# Dry and hot tails: in the year, and cumulative with lags.
TAIL_CELLS <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cell, ~variable, ~deviation, ~level_index,
  "P -3 SD, 0.5 m", "RR", -3, 1L,
  "P -3 SD, 1.5 m", "RR", -3, 2L,
  "T +3 SD, 25 °C", "TM", 3, 3L
)
tail_summary <- function(f) {
  d5 <- add_deviation_lags(f, 5L)
  lags5 <- unlist(lapply(1:5, function(k) c(lag_terms("TM", k), lag_terms("RR", k))))
  m5 <- fit_model(c(preferred_terms, lags5), d5)
  d10 <- add_deviation_lags(f, 10L)
  m10 <- fit_model(c(restricted_terms("TM", 10L), restricted_terms("RR", 10L), CONTROLS), d10)
  effects <- bind_rows(
    mutate(climate_effects(f), horizon = "year"),
    mutate(filter(cumulative_effects(m5, f$panel$label, FALSE, 5L), through == 5), horizon = "5 years"),
    mutate(filter(cumulative_effects(m10, f$panel$label, TRUE, 10L), through == 10),
           horizon = "10 years")
  )
  effects %>%
    inner_join(TAIL_CELLS, by = c("variable", "deviation", "level_index")) %>%
    transmute(panel = f$source_panel, sample = f$sample,
              column = paste0(cell, ": ", horizon),
              value = sprintf("%+.2f%s", 100 * estimate, stars(p_value))) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = value)
}
bind_rows(lapply(outlier_fits, tail_summary)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Dry and hot tails by outlier sample (pp of GDP per capita): in the",
                               "year, cumulative over five years (unrestricted lags) and ten years",
                               "(common interaction); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))
```

# Warming scenario: one set of coefficients, three deviation definitions

Three warming paths, with no natural variability and each country's SD
unchanged:

- gradual: a linear warming of 0.2 °C a decade until +1 °C (50 years), then
  constant for 30 years;
- step: +1 °C at once, then constant for 30 years;
- pulse: +1 °C for one year, then back to the pre-warming climate (30 years
  after).

Precipitation is unchanged (dP = 0). The temperature coefficients are those of
the preferred model (PWT x ERA5) in every case, so the three definitions differ
only in how the warming becomes a deviation and in the long-run climate of the
interaction:

```text
(a) horizon:                          dT_t = W_t / sd_all,          climate T0
(b) 20-year, horizon interaction:     dT_t = (W_t - W20_t) / sd_20, climate T0
(c) 20-year, matched interaction:     dT_t = (W_t - W20_t) / sd_20, climate T0 + W20_t
```

where W_t is the warming in year t, W20_t its mean over the 20 years before t
(zero before the warming starts; after the pulse, the years back at T0 are
below W20_t, so they enter the cold arm), T0 the pre-warming climate (the horizon
mean), and sd_all and sd_20 the horizon and trailing 20-year SDs. The growth
effect in year t is the preferred form's temperature terms at dT_t and the
climate; the cumulative effect through year K is their sum over years 1..K (the
effect on the level of GDP per capita, in log points x 100), with 95% CIs by the
delta method (errors clustered by country).

Typical cold, average and hot country: the terciles of the countries of
PWT x ERA5 by long-run temperature; within each, the median long-run
temperature, horizon SD, and trailing 20-year SD (each country's median over
its years).

The model was estimated on deviations with each unit's mean and quadratic trend
removed, i.e. on year-to-year deviations around the unit's trend; applying it
to a sustained shift extrapolates those responses.

```{r warming-scenario, fig.width=13, fig.height=7}
WARMING_TOTAL <- 1       # °C
YEARS_AFTER <- 30L       # years after +1 °C is reached
TRAILING <- 20L          # years of the trailing mean of the 20-year definition

# Each path: the warming above the pre-warming climate in years 1, 2, ... and
# the year +1 °C is reached.
gradual_path <- function(rate_per_decade) {
  reach <- as.integer(round(10 * WARMING_TOTAL / rate_per_decade))
  list(warming = pmin(rate_per_decade / 10 * seq_len(reach + YEARS_AFTER), WARMING_TOTAL),
       reach = reach)
}
WARMING_PATHS <- list(
  "Gradual: 0.2 C a decade to +1 C, then constant" = gradual_path(0.2),
  "Step: +1 C at once, then constant" = list(warming = rep(WARMING_TOTAL, 1L + YEARS_AFTER),
                                             reach = 1L),
  "Pulse: +1 C for one year" = list(warming = c(WARMING_TOTAL, rep(0, YEARS_AFTER)), reach = 1L)
)
# Mean of the warming over the TRAILING years before each year (zero before year 1).
trailing_mean <- function(warming) {
  padded <- c(rep(0, TRAILING), warming)
  vapply(seq_along(warming), function(t) mean(padded[t:(t + TRAILING - 1)]), 0)
}

countries <- main$clean %>%
  group_by(GID_1) %>%
  summarise(T0 = first(mean_TM_all), sd_all = first(sd_TM_all),
            sd_20 = stats::median(sd_TM_lag_20), .groups = "drop")
countries$type <- cut(countries$T0, stats::quantile(countries$T0, c(0, 1 / 3, 2 / 3, 1)),
                      labels = c("Cold", "Average", "Hot"), include.lowest = TRUE)
typical <- countries %>%
  group_by(type) %>%
  summarise(countries = n(), T_range = sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", min(T0), max(T0)),
            T0 = stats::median(T0), sd_all = stats::median(sd_all),
            sd_20 = stats::median(sd_20), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(warming_sd_all = WARMING_TOTAL / sd_all, warming_sd_20 = WARMING_TOTAL / sd_20)

typical %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste("Typical countries (terciles of PWT x ERA5 by long-run temperature,",
                               "medians): long-run temperature (C), SDs (C) and +1 C in SDs"))

SCENARIOS <- c("(a) Horizon", "(b) 20-year, horizon interaction",
               "(c) 20-year, matched interaction")
# Deviation (SD) and long-run climate (C) of each year of `warming` under
# definition `s`.
scenario_path <- function(s, warming, T0, sd_all, sd_20) {
  trailing <- trailing_mean(warming)
  fixed <- rep(T0, length(warming))
  switch(s,
         "(a) Horizon" = list(deviation = warming / sd_all, climate = fixed),
         "(b) 20-year, horizon interaction" = list(deviation = (warming - trailing) / sd_20,
                                                   climate = fixed),
         "(c) 20-year, matched interaction" = list(deviation = (warming - trailing) / sd_20,
                                                   climate = T0 + trailing))
}

scenario_model <- selection_models[[PREFERRED_DEFINITION]][[PREFERRED_FORM]]
scenario_terms <- names(stats::coef(scenario_model))
# Growth effect of each year (rows) as weights on the coefficients.
year_weights <- function(path) {
  t(mapply(function(x, m) {
    w <- stats::setNames(numeric(length(scenario_terms)), scenario_terms)
    for (s in FORMS[[PREFERRED_FORM]][["TM"]]) {
      term <- paste0("devTM", s)
      w[[term]] <- term_value(s, x)
      w[[interaction_name(term, "clim_TM", scenario_terms)]] <- term_value(s, x) * m
    }
    w
  }, path$deviation, path$climate))
}

scenario_effects <- bind_rows(lapply(names(WARMING_PATHS), function(p) {
  warming <- WARMING_PATHS[[p]]$warming
  bind_rows(lapply(SCENARIOS, function(s) {
    bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(typical)), function(i) {
      # (Not called `path`: mutate() below creates a column of that name.)
      dev_path <- scenario_path(s, warming, typical$T0[i], typical$sd_all[i], typical$sd_20[i])
      W <- year_weights(dev_path)
      colnames(W) <- scenario_terms
      cumulative <- apply(W, 2, cumsum)
      bind_rows(
        mutate(linear_combination(scenario_model, W), quantity = "year"),
        mutate(linear_combination(scenario_model, cumulative), quantity = "cumulative")
      ) %>%
        mutate(path = p, scenario = s, type = as.character(typical$type[i]),
               year = rep(seq_along(warming), 2), deviation = rep(dev_path$deviation, 2),
               climate = rep(dev_path$climate, 2),
               p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)))
    }))
  }))
}))

# Cumulative effect when +1 °C is reached and 10, 20 and 30 years after.
REPORT_AFTER <- c(0L, 10L, 20L, YEARS_AFTER)
scenario_effects %>%
  filter(quantity == "cumulative") %>%
  mutate(after = year - vapply(WARMING_PATHS[path], `[[`, 0L, "reach")) %>%
  filter(after %in% REPORT_AFTER) %>%
  mutate(cell = sprintf("%+.1f [%+.1f, %+.1f]%s", 100 * estimate, 100 * conf_low,
                        100 * conf_high, stars(p_value)),
         column = factor(ifelse(after == 0, "+1 C reached", sprintf("%d years after", after)),
                         levels = c("+1 C reached", sprintf("%d years after", REPORT_AFTER[-1])))) %>%
  select(path, scenario, type, column, cell) %>%
  arrange(column) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = cell) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Cumulative effect of the warming on GDP per capita (log points x 100, 95% CI), with the ",
    "coefficients of the preferred model (", PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION,
    "); +1 C is reached in year ", WARMING_PATHS[[1]]$reach, " (gradual) or year 1 (step, ",
    "pulse); *** p < 0.01, ** p < 0.05, * p < 0.1"))

QUANTITY_LABELS <- c(deviation = "Deviation (SD)",
                     cumulative = "Cumulative effect (log points x 100)")
plot_scenario <- function(p) {
  plot_data <- bind_rows(
    scenario_effects %>%
      filter(path == p, quantity == "year") %>%
      transmute(scenario, type, year, quantity = "deviation", estimate = deviation,
                conf_low = NA_real_, conf_high = NA_real_),
    scenario_effects %>%
      filter(path == p, quantity == "cumulative") %>%
      transmute(scenario, type, year, quantity = "cumulative", estimate = 100 * estimate,
                conf_low = 100 * conf_low, conf_high = 100 * conf_high)
  ) %>%
    mutate(quantity = factor(QUANTITY_LABELS[quantity], levels = QUANTITY_LABELS),
           scenario = factor(scenario, levels = SCENARIOS),
           type = sprintf("%s country (%.1f C; SD %.2f horizon, %.2f 20-year)", type,
                          typical$T0[match(type, as.character(typical$type))],
                          typical$sd_all[match(type, as.character(typical$type))],
                          typical$sd_20[match(type, as.character(typical$type))])) %>%
    mutate(type = factor(type, levels = unique(type)))

  ggplot(plot_data, aes(year, estimate, colour = scenario, fill = scenario)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = WARMING_PATHS[[p]]$reach, colour = GRID_MUTED, linewidth = 0.3,
               linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = conf_low, ymax = conf_high), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA,
                data = filter(plot_data, !is.na(conf_low))) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
    facet_grid(quantity ~ type, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = grid_colours(SCENARIOS), name = NULL) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = grid_colours(SCENARIOS), name = NULL) +
    labs(x = "Year from the start of the warming", y = NULL,
         title = paste0(p, ": one set of coefficients, three deviation definitions"),
         subtitle = wrap_text(paste0(
           "Coefficients of the preferred model (", PREFERRED_FORM, ", ", PREFERRED_DEFINITION,
           " deviations, PWT x ERA5). No natural variability; SDs unchanged; precipitation ",
           "unchanged. Top: the temperature deviation ((b) and (c) share it); bottom: the ",
           "cumulative effect on GDP per capita. Dotted line: +1 C reached. Shaded: 95% CI ",
           "(clustered by country)."), 175)) +
    theme_results() +
    theme(strip.placement = "outside")
}
for (p in names(WARMING_PATHS)) print(plot_scenario(p))
```

# Where shocks matter: robustness by country

For every national panel (PWT and World Bank with ERA5, CRU TS and UDelaware),
every deviation definition interacted with the horizon mean (horizon, 20-year
and the two mixes) and every arms form (linear, quadratic and the two mixes),
6 x 4 x 4 = 96 fits, each on its own rows: the effect on growth that year of a
cold (dry) and a hot (wet) shock in each country, at its recent climate.

- The shock is three times the SD of the country's last 10 years of the panel
  (°C or m), converted to the deviation units of the fit: divided by the
  country's horizon SD, or by its trailing 20-year SD of the last year. The
  same physical shock in every fit.
- The long-run climate of the interaction is the country's mean of the same 10
  years.
- Each panel uses its own climate data for both.

The maps show the effect of the shock in the preferred model (PWT x ERA5), and
its robustness across the 96 fits by pattern, against the sign of the
preferred estimate:

- plain fill: the estimate has that sign (significant or not) in more than 80%
  of the fits; with a thick border if it is also significant at 5% with that
  sign in more than 80% of them;
- dots: otherwise, the estimate has that sign in more than 50% of the fits;
- stripes: neither.

Countries outside the PWT x ERA5 sample are grey. The table lists the countries
with a thick border, ranked by recent mean climate.

```{r robust-shocks, fig.width=14, fig.height=8.5}
RECENT_YEARS <- 10L
SHOCK_SD <- 3
PLAIN_SIGN <- 0.8        # plain fill: share of fits with the preferred sign
DOTS_SIGN <- 0.5         # dots: share of fits with the preferred sign
BORDER_SIGNIFICANT <- 0.8 # thick border: share of fits significant with the preferred sign
PATTERN_SPACING <- 250e3 # metres between dots and between stripes (Robinson projection)
ROBINSON <- "+proj=robin"
SHOCK_DEFINITIONS <- names(DEFINITIONS)[!grepl("matched", names(DEFINITIONS))]

# Each country's climate over the last RECENT_YEARS years of the panel (mean
# and SD of each variable), and the SDs of the two deviation baselines (horizon,
# and the trailing 20 years of the last year).
recent_climate <- function(panel) {
  panel$data %>%
    filter(GID_0 %in% panel$clean$GID_0, year > panel$end_year - RECENT_YEARS,
           year <= panel$end_year, !is.na(TM), !is.na(RR)) %>%
    group_by(GID_0) %>%
    filter(n() == RECENT_YEARS) %>%
    summarise(mean_TM = mean(TM), sd_TM = sd(TM), mean_RR = mean(RR), sd_RR = sd(RR),
              sd_TM_all = first(sd_TM_all), sd_RR_all = first(sd_RR_all),
              sd_TM_lag_20 = sd_TM_lag_20[which.max(year)],
              sd_RR_lag_20 = sd_RR_lag_20[which.max(year)], .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(sd_TM_lag_20 > 0, sd_RR_lag_20 > 0)
}

# Effect of a shock of -/+ SHOCK_SD recent SDs in each country of `rc`, in a
# model of `form` with deviations of definition `def`.
shock_effects <- function(model, form, def, rc) {
  terms <- names(stats::coef(model))
  bind_rows(lapply(c("TM", "RR"), function(v) {
    grid <- expand.grid(i = seq_len(nrow(rc)), sign = c(-1, 1))
    sd_fit <- rc[[paste0("sd_", v, "_", DEFINITIONS[[def]][[v]])]][grid$i]
    x <- grid$sign * SHOCK_SD * rc[[paste0("sd_", v)]][grid$i] / sd_fit
    m <- rc[[paste0("mean_", v)]][grid$i]
    G <- matrix(0, nrow(grid), length(terms), dimnames = list(NULL, terms))
    for (s in FORMS[[form]][[v]]) {
      term <- paste0("dev", v, s)
      G[, term] <- term_value(s, x)
      G[, interaction_name(term, paste0("clim_", v), terms)] <- term_value(s, x) * m
    }
    linear_combination(model, G) %>%
      mutate(GID_0 = rc$GID_0[grid$i], variable = v,
             shock = ifelse(grid$sign < 0, "negative", "positive"),
             p_value = 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(estimate / std_error)))
  }))
}

recent <- lapply(national_panels, recent_climate)
shock_fits <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_along(national_panels), function(j) {
  p <- national_panels[[j]]
  bind_rows(lapply(SHOCK_DEFINITIONS, function(def) {
    d <- add_deviation_terms(p$clean, DEFINITIONS[[def]])
    bind_rows(lapply(ARMS, function(f) {
      shock_effects(fit_model(form_terms(FORMS[[f]]), d), f, def, recent[[j]]) %>%
        mutate(panel = p$label, definition = def, form = f)
    }))
  }))
}))

SHOCK_FACETS <- tibble::tibble(
  variable = c("TM", "TM", "RR", "RR"), shock = c("negative", "positive", "negative", "positive"),
  facet = c("Temperature: cold shock (-3 recent SD)", "Temperature: hot shock (+3 recent SD)",
            "Precipitation: dry shock (-3 recent SD)", "Precipitation: wet shock (+3 recent SD)")
)
# Recent climate of each country, averaged over the panels that have it.
recent_mean <- bind_rows(recent) %>%
  group_by(GID_0) %>%
  summarise(across(c(mean_TM, sd_TM, mean_RR, sd_RR), mean), .groups = "drop")
# The shock in the preferred model (PWT x ERA5, at its recent climate), and the
# agreement of the 96 fits with the sign of that estimate.
preferred_shock <- shock_effects(selection_models[[PREFERRED_DEFINITION]][[PREFERRED_FORM]],
                                 PREFERRED_FORM, PREFERRED_DEFINITION, recent[[1]]) %>%
  select(GID_0, variable, shock, preferred = estimate, preferred_p = p_value)
shock_summary <- shock_fits %>%
  inner_join(preferred_shock, by = c("GID_0", "variable", "shock")) %>%
  group_by(GID_0, variable, shock, preferred, preferred_p) %>%
  summarise(fits = n(),
            robust = mean(p_value < 0.05 & sign(estimate) == sign(preferred)),
            same_sign = mean(sign(estimate) == sign(preferred)), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(pattern = case_when(same_sign > PLAIN_SIGN ~ "fill", same_sign > DOTS_SIGN ~ "dots",
                             TRUE ~ "stripes"),
         border = pattern == "fill" & robust > BORDER_SIGNIFICANT) %>%
  inner_join(SHOCK_FACETS, by = c("variable", "shock")) %>%
  left_join(recent_mean, by = "GID_0")

world <- rnaturalearth::ne_countries(scale = "small", returnclass = "sf") %>%
  mutate(GID_0 = ifelse(iso_a3 == "-99", adm0_a3, iso_a3)) %>%
  filter(GID_0 != "ATA") %>%
  select(GID_0, geometry) %>%
  sf::st_transform(ROBINSON) %>%
  sf::st_make_valid()
# (rbind, not bind_rows(): it keeps the sf class.)
shock_map <- do.call(rbind, lapply(SHOCK_FACETS$facet, function(f) {
  world %>%
    left_join(filter(shock_summary, facet == f) %>% select(GID_0, preferred, pattern, border),
              by = "GID_0") %>%
    mutate(facet = factor(f, levels = SHOCK_FACETS$facet))
}))

# Patterns as ordinary geometries, built once (fast to draw, unlike pattern
# fills): a regular grid of dots kept inside the dotted countries, and diagonal
# lines clipped to the striped ones.
box <- sf::st_bbox(world)
height <- box[["ymax"]] - box[["ymin"]]
dot_grid <- sf::st_sf(geometry = sf::st_make_grid(world, cellsize = PATTERN_SPACING,
                                                  what = "centers"))
stripe_lines <- sf::st_sfc(lapply(
  seq(box[["xmin"]] - height, box[["xmax"]], by = PATTERN_SPACING * sqrt(2)),
  function(x0) sf::st_linestring(rbind(c(x0, box[["ymin"]]), c(x0 + height, box[["ymax"]])))
), crs = sf::st_crs(world))
pattern_layer <- function(kind) {
  layers <- lapply(SHOCK_FACETS$facet, function(f) {
    polygons <- shock_map[shock_map$facet == f & shock_map$pattern %in% kind, ]
    if (!nrow(polygons)) return(NULL)
    geometry <- if (kind == "dots") {
      sf::st_geometry(dot_grid)[lengths(sf::st_intersects(dot_grid, polygons)) > 0]
    } else {
      sf::st_collection_extract(sf::st_intersection(stripe_lines, sf::st_union(polygons)),
                                "LINESTRING")
    }
    if (!length(geometry)) return(NULL)
    sf::st_sf(facet = factor(f, levels = SHOCK_FACETS$facet), geometry = geometry)
  })
  do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), layers))
}
dots <- pattern_layer("dots")
stripes <- pattern_layer("stripes")

fill_limit <- stats::quantile(abs(100 * shock_summary$preferred), 0.98, names = FALSE)
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = shock_map, aes(fill = 100 * preferred), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.1) +
  (if (!is.null(stripes)) geom_sf(data = stripes, colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.2)) +
  (if (!is.null(dots)) geom_sf(data = dots, colour = "grey15", size = 0.35, shape = 16)) +
  geom_sf(data = shock_map[shock_map$border %in% TRUE, ], fill = NA, colour = "grey10",
          linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~facet, nrow = 2) +
  coord_sf(crs = ROBINSON, expand = FALSE, datum = NA) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#c0392b", mid = "#f2f1ec", high = GRID_PALETTE[[1]], midpoint = 0,
                       limits = c(-fill_limit, fill_limit), oob = scales::squish,
                       na.value = "grey85",
                       name = "Effect on growth that year,\npreferred model (pp)") +
  labs(title = "Effect of a shock in the preferred model, and its robustness across specifications and datasets",
       subtitle = wrap_text(paste0(
         "Effect that year of a shock of ", SHOCK_SD, " SDs of the country's last ", RECENT_YEARS,
         " years, at the mean climate of those years: ", PREFERRED_FORM, ", ",
         PREFERRED_DEFINITION, " deviations, PWT x ERA5 (colour scale capped at the 98th ",
         "percentile). Robustness across the fits (up to ",
         length(national_panels) * length(SHOCK_DEFINITIONS) * length(ARMS), ": ",
         length(national_panels), " national panels x ", length(SHOCK_DEFINITIONS),
         " deviation definitions x ", length(ARMS), " arms forms), against the sign of the ",
         "preferred estimate: plain, that sign in more than ", 100 * PLAIN_SIGN, "% of them ",
         "(thick border: also significant at 5% in more than ", 100 * BORDER_SIGNIFICANT,
         "%); dots, that sign in more than ", 100 * DOTS_SIGN, "%; stripes, neither. Grey: ",
         "outside the PWT x ERA5 sample."), 170)) +
  theme_results() +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), legend.key.width = grid::unit(2.5, "cm"))

# Countries with a thick border, ranked by recent mean climate.
shock_summary %>%
  filter(border) %>%
  mutate(country = countrycode::countrycode(GID_0, "iso3c", "country.name", warn = FALSE),
         recent_mean = ifelse(variable == "TM", mean_TM, mean_RR),
         recent_sd = ifelse(variable == "TM", sd_TM, sd_RR),
         facet = factor(facet, levels = SHOCK_FACETS$facet)) %>%
  arrange(facet, recent_mean) %>%
  transmute(shock = facet, country, preferred_pp = round(100 * preferred, 2),
            preferred_p = signif(preferred_p, 2), robust_share = round(robust, 2), fits,
            recent_mean = round(recent_mean, 2), recent_sd = round(recent_sd, 2)) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = paste0(
    "Countries where the shock is significant (5%) with the sign of the preferred estimate in ",
    "more than ", 100 * BORDER_SIGNIFICANT, "% of their fits (thick border), by shock, ranked ",
    "by the mean climate of ",
    "the last ", RECENT_YEARS, " years (°C or m a year, averaged over the panels; SD of the ",
    "same years)"))

# Countries by pattern.
shock_summary %>%
  mutate(pattern = factor(ifelse(border, "fill, thick border", pattern),
                          levels = c("fill, thick border", "fill", "dots", "stripes"))) %>%
  count(facet = factor(facet, levels = SHOCK_FACETS$facet), pattern, .drop = FALSE) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = pattern, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Countries of the PWT x ERA5 sample by robustness pattern")
```
